title: Jesus College Cambridge Research Fellowships 2027 | 3-Year Fellowships in UK
summary: Jesus College, University of Cambridge is inviting applications for three Research Fellowships for early-career researchers who are nearing completion of their PhD or have recently started their postdoctoral careers. The fellowships provide an opportunity to spend three years developing research within the academic environment of the University of Cambridge , with a starting remuneration of £32,882 , additional benefits and research support. Two of the fellowships are available across selected Arts and Humanities subjects , while one fellowship is available in the Sciences . About the Jesus College Research Fellowships The Research Fellowships are designed for researchers at the early stages of their academic careers. The fellowships are normally three years in duration and are expected to commence on 1 October 2027 . The opportunity is particularly suitable for candidates who are: Graduate students in the latter stages of research leading to a PhD; or Postdoctoral researchers who have recently been awarded their PhD. Jesus College notes that candidates who have undertaken more than five years of full-time research are unlikely to be considered . However, the College may consider exceptions where candidates are able to present a case explaining their circumstances as part of the application. Research Fellowship Areas Arts Research Fellowships Two Research Fellowships are available in the following subject areas: Anglo-Saxon, Norse and Celtic (ASNC) Education Studies English Law Modern Languages Theology Applicants should ensure that their proposed research fits clearly within one of the advertised subject areas. Science Research Fellowship A separate Research Fellowship is available in the Sciences . The Science fellowship provides an opportunity for an early-career researcher to develop their research within the Cambridge academic environment. Who Should Apply? The fellowships are intended for brilliant early-career researchers who are beginning to establish themselves as independent scholars. Applicants may be: Current PhD students who are approaching completion of their doctoral research. Researchers who have recently completed a PhD. Early-career postdoctoral researchers. Candidates who have undertaken more than five years of full-time research are generally unlikely to be considered, although exceptions may be possible. The College is looking for researchers who can demonstrate the importance and potential of their current and proposed research. Fellowship Benefits Successful candidates will receive several financial and academic benefits throughout the fellowship. £32,882 Starting Remuneration The remuneration for a Research Fellow is determined by reference to the University of Cambridge salary scale and starts at £32,882 . Three-Year Fellowship The fellowship provides funding and support for three years , normally commencing on 1 October 2027 . This gives early-career researchers valuable time to develop their research, publications and academic profile. Free Meals Research Fellows receive a free dinner or lunch at Jesus College, regardless of whether they live in College or elsewhere. Research Benefits Certain research-related expenses may be reimbursed, providing additional support for fellows undertaking their academic work. Pension Research Fellows may also be eligible to join the University Pension Scheme . Application Requirements Candidates will need to complete the application process through the Jesus College Research Fellowship application system. Applications must include the required information and supporting materials. Shortlisted candidates will subsequently be asked to provide: One sample of written work , up to a maximum of 40,000 words . A 500-word statement explaining the importance of their current and proposed research. Reports from two referees . Applicants should therefore begin preparing their research materials and contacting potential referees well ahead of the deadline. What Should Your Research Statement Demonstrate? The 500-word statement provides shortlisted candidates with an opportunity to explain why their research matters. Applicants should use this space to clearly communicate: The significance of their current research. The direction of their proposed research. Why the proposed work is important. How their research could contribute to their academic field. Their potential as an early-career researcher. A clear and focused research proposal can help demonstrate the intellectual value and future potential of the candidate s work. Application Timeline Applications Open: 3 August 2026 Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 Closing Time: 5:00 PM Fellowship Start Date: 1 October 2027 Duration: Three years Location: Jesus College, Cambridge, United Kingdom How to Apply Applications are submitted online through the Jesus College Research Fellowship application portal. Application Portal Apply through the Jesus College Research Fellowship Portal Applicants can also find additional information about the vacancies and fellowship opportunities on the College s official website. Jesus College Vacancies and Fellowships Important Information for Applicants Candidates should carefully review the official fellowship details before applying. In particular, applicants should consider their career stage. These fellowships are specifically intended for early-career researchers , and candidates with more than five years of full-time research are unlikely to be considered unless they can provide a convincing explanation for an exception. Shortlisted applicants should also be prepared to submit substantial written work of up to 40,000 words and a concise 500-word research statement . It is therefore advisable to prepare application materials well before the deadline and ensure that referees have sufficient time to submit their reports. Why Apply? The Jesus College Research Fellowships provide an opportunity for emerging researchers to develop their academic careers within one of the world s most recognised university environments. Beyond the financial remuneration, fellows can benefit from the College s academic community, research support and opportunities to interact with researchers across different disciplines. For researchers transitioning from doctoral study into independent research, a three-year fellowship can provide valuable time to strengthen their research portfolio, develop publications and establish themselves within their field. Conclusion The Jesus College Cambridge Research Fellowships 2027 offer three early-career researchers the opportunity to undertake supported research at Jesus College, University of Cambridge . With a starting remuneration of £32,882 , a three-year fellowship, research-related benefits, free College meals and potential access to the University Pension Scheme, the opportunity provides substantial support for researchers at the beginning of their academic careers. The fellowships are open across the Sciences, ASNC, Education Studies, English, Law, Modern Languages and Theology , making the opportunity relevant to researchers from a range of academic disciplines. If you are completing your PhD or have recently received your doctorate and are looking for an opportunity to develop your research in Cambridge, this fellowship is worth considering. Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 at 5:00 PM. Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage . title: 2027 Peter McMullin Centre Visiting Fellowship on Statelessness: Up to AUD 6,000 in Funding for International Researchers and Practitioners
summary: Applications are now open for the 2027 Visiting Fellowship Scheme at the Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness , offering researchers, practitioners and educators an opportunity to spend time at the Centre, undertake research related to statelessness and develop international academic and professional collaborations. The funded fellowship provides up to AUD 6,000 to support international travel and accommodation costs in Melbourne. The fellowship is expected to last approximately one to two months and can be undertaken between August and October 2027 . The opportunity is particularly relevant to researchers and professionals working on statelessness, nationality, citizenship, displacement, migration, human rights, international law and related areas. 2027 Peter McMullin Centre Visiting Fellowship at a Glance Detail Information Host Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness Institution Melbourne Law School, University of Melbourne Opportunity Visiting Research Fellowship Year 2027 Funding Up to AUD 6,000 Duration Suggested 1–2 months Visit period August–October 2027 Location Melbourne, Australia Research area Statelessness and related issues Application deadline 30 November 2026 Application format One PDF document Visa/insurance International visitors are responsible for their own visa and insurance costs About the Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness The Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness is based at Melbourne Law School, University of Melbourne , and focuses on research, education and collaboration relating to statelessness. Its Visiting Fellowship Scheme provides an opportunity for people working on statelessness to engage directly with the Centre s work while developing research collaborations and international professional networks. The fellowship is designed not simply as a period of independent research, but as an opportunity for Visiting Fellows to become involved in the intellectual and professional activities of the Centre during their stay. What Does the Funded Fellowship Offer? The 2027 funded Visiting Fellowship provides financial assistance of up to AUD 6,000 . The funding can support: International travel to Melbourne Accommodation in Melbourne during the fellowship Other eligible costs associated with undertaking the visit, subject to the proposed budget Applicants must provide a detailed breakdown of the amount requested. If airfare is required, applicants should include the estimated airfare cost in their budget. The maximum amount available is AUD 6,000 . Fellowship Duration and Timing The suggested duration of the fellowship is one to two months . The funded fellowship is available to be undertaken between: August and October 2027. Applicants should therefore propose their preferred dates within this period as part of their application. What Will Visiting Fellows Do? Visiting Fellows are expected to participate actively in the life and work of the Peter McMullin Centre during their stay. This can include: Conducting research related to statelessness Developing research collaborations Participating in Centre events Attending workshops Engaging with researchers and other Centre members Sharing research ideas and expertise Contributing to discussions relevant to statelessness research The fellowship is therefore suitable for individuals who want more than simply access to a workspace while conducting independent research. Workspace and Research Facilities Visiting Fellows will be provided with a workspace during their stay. They will also have access to: Library facilities Computer facilities Centre activities Events and workshops These resources can support researchers in conducting their proposed research while being based in Melbourne. Research Presentation Requirement As part of the fellowship, Visiting Fellows are expected to share their research with the Centre and wider audiences. Depending on the nature of their work, fellows will present their research through: A Faculty seminar A public seminar A work-in-progress meeting This provides fellows with an opportunity to receive feedback, discuss their research with other academics and professionals, and contribute to intellectual exchange at the Centre. Contribution to the Critical Statelessness Studies Blog Visiting Fellows are also expected, where appropriate, to contribute a blog post to the Critical Statelessness Studies blog . This provides an additional opportunity to communicate research findings, ideas or insights to a broader audience interested in statelessness and related issues. Who Can Apply for the Fellowship? The Centre explicitly recognises that statelessness research and professional work are undertaken by people in different career stages and professional settings. Applications are welcomed from: Postdoctoral researchers Early-career researchers Established academics Tenured academics Statelessness practitioners Non-academic professionals Educators Researchers with lived experience of statelessness The Centre particularly states that researchers with lived experience of statelessness are strongly encouraged to apply . Non-Academic Applicants Are Also Eligible Importantly, the fellowship is not restricted to university academics. Non-academic visiting professionals can also be considered if they propose an applied research project that is relevant to the work of the Centre. This makes the opportunity potentially suitable for professionals working in areas such as: Human rights Refugee protection Migration Nationality and citizenship Legal practice Policy Advocacy International development Statelessness-related programmes The proposed project must demonstrate relevance to the Centre s work. What Must Be Included in the Application? Applications for the funded fellowship must be submitted as one PDF document containing the required materials. Applicants need to provide the following: 1. Curriculum Vitae and Publications List Applicants should include their CV along with a list of their publications. This allows the selection team to understand the applicant s academic, research or professional background and previous work. 2. Research Plan A research plan of no more than 1,000 words is required. The research plan should explain: The research the applicant intends to undertake The purpose and objectives of the research Proposed activities during the visit Potential collaborations How the applicant intends to contribute to the work of the Centre Applicants should demonstrate a clear connection between their proposed research and the Centre s focus on statelessness. 3. Proposed Fellowship Dates Applicants must indicate their proposed dates for the visit . For the funded 2027 fellowship, the visit should fall within the available August–October 2027 period. 4. Funding Request and Budget Applicants must state the amount of funding they are requesting, up to the maximum of: AUD 6,000 A detailed budget breakdown must accompany the request. Where international air travel is required, the budget should include the estimated cost of airfare. 5. Reference Letter Applicants must provide one letter of reference . For non-academic applicants, the Centre accepts a letter of support from an employer or another organisation or entity with which the applicant is professionally associated . How to Apply Applications should be submitted by email to: law-statelessness@unimelb.edu.au The email subject line should be: Visiting Fellowship Application Applicants should submit the complete application as one PDF document . Questions about the fellowship can also be directed to the same email address. Application Deadline The deadline for applications for the 2027 funded Visiting Fellowship is 30 November 2026 . Applicants should ensure that their complete application is submitted before the deadline. Important Information for International Applicants Applicants travelling to Australia from outside the country are responsible for obtaining and paying for any necessary: Australian visa Travel documentation Insurance These costs are separate from the fellowship funding arrangements and applicants should take them into account when planning their visit. Self-Funded Visiting Fellowship Option The Centre also welcomes applicants who are able to fund their own visit . Self-funded visitors can apply to visit the Centre throughout the year. Subject to availability, self-funded visitors may receive: Workspace Library access Computer access Opportunities to participate in Centre events Opportunities to participate in workshops Engagement with the Centre s academic and professional community Unlike the funded fellowship, self-funded visits do not have the 30 November 2026 deadline. Applications for self-funded visits can be made year-round . Requirements for Self-Funded Visitors Self-funded applicants should provide: Curriculum vitae and publications list Research plan of up to 1,000 words Proposed dates of the visit One letter of reference For non-academic visitors, the reference can be a letter of support from their employer or another professionally associated organisation. Funded vs Self-Funded Visit Feature Funded Fellowship Self-Funded Visit Funding Up to AUD 6,000 No Centre funding stated Research focus Statelessness-related research Relevant research Duration Suggested 1–2 months Proposed by visitor Visit period August–October 2027 Year-round applications Workspace Yes Subject to availability Library access Yes Yes Computer access Yes Yes Centre participation Expected Encouraged Research plan Required Required CV/publications Required Required Reference Required Required Deadline 30 November 2026 Year-round Examples of Previous Visiting Fellows The Centre has hosted Visiting Fellows from a wide range of academic and professional backgrounds and countries. Previous fellows have researched topics including: Statelessness and citizenship Statelessness among Rohingya communities Statelessness in the Middle East and North Africa Statelessness in Australia and New Zealand Climate displacement and nationality Statelessness and gender Statelessness among Roma communities Childhood statelessness Legal clinics addressing statelessness Denial of identity documents Statelessness and migration Statelessness and nationality laws Statelessness among displaced populations The list of previous fellows demonstrates the broad range of disciplines and geographic contexts that can be connected to statelessness research. A Globally Oriented Fellowship Previous Visiting Fellows have come from institutions and organisations in countries including: Australia Austria Belgium Germany India Italy Myanmar New Zealand Pakistan Poland Singapore Thailand The Netherlands United Kingdom United States The Centre s previous fellowship cohort also demonstrates that statelessness can be studied from multiple disciplinary perspectives, including law, political science, sociology, anthropology, history, philosophy and professional practice. Why This Fellowship Is Valuable The Peter McMullin Centre Visiting Fellowship can provide researchers and professionals with an opportunity to spend dedicated time developing a statelessness-related research project while engaging with an international research community. The combination of funding, research facilities and collaboration can be particularly valuable for applicants who want to: Advance an existing research project Develop a new research collaboration Work with researchers specialising in statelessness Receive feedback on research Present their work to an academic or public audience Build international professional connections Explore applied research approaches Contribute to global discussions on statelessness The opportunity also provides a platform for researchers to bring perspectives from their own countries, communities and professional environments into international statelessness research. Click HERE to read more and Apply. Conclusion The 2027 Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness Visiting Fellowship is a funded research opportunity for academics, researchers, practitioners and educators working on statelessness or closely related issues. The selected funded Visiting Fellow can receive up to AUD 6,000 toward international travel and accommodation in Melbourne and undertake a suggested one- to two-month research visit between August and October 2027 . During the fellowship, the Visiting Fellow will have access to workspace, library and computer facilities and will be expected to participate actively in the Centre s activities, present their research and contribute to the Centre s broader intellectual community. The opportunity is open across career stages, from postdoctoral early-career researchers to established and tenured academics , while relevant non-academic professionals are also encouraged to apply. Researchers with lived experience of statelessness are particularly encouraged to submit applications. For those interested in conducting research related to statelessness while developing international collaborations, the fellowship offers a valuable opportunity to engage with a specialist research centre in Melbourne. Application deadline: 30 November 2026. Click HERE for more fellowship opportunities. title: PERIL Youth Advisory Council 2026: Apply to Shape Research on Online Harms, Polarization, Misogyny and Extremism
summary: The PERIL Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is now accepting applications from young people aged 18 to 24 who want to contribute their perspectives to research on online culture and emerging challenges affecting young people. The Youth Advisory Council brings together 8–10 young people who meet virtually every two to three months to discuss issues such as online polarization, online harms, misogyny, extremism and other emerging trends in digital culture. This is a low-lift volunteer opportunity designed to give young people a meaningful voice in research without requiring a major time commitment outside scheduled meetings. Council members bring their lived experiences and perspectives, while PERIL brings its research and expertise. Together, they work toward research and solutions that better reflect the realities facing young people today. What Is the PERIL Youth Advisory Council? The Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is an advisory group established by PERIL to ensure that research and proposed solutions are informed by the experiences and perspectives of young people. The council consists of approximately 8–10 young people between the ages of 18 and 24 . Members meet virtually every 2–3 months and contribute their perspectives on developments in online culture and issues affecting young people. The council may provide feedback on: Research questions Research findings Proposed solutions Emerging issues and trends Concerns affecting young people How research reflects Gen Z experiences The goal is to ensure that PERIL s work is not developed without considering the voices of the people most directly affected by the rapidly changing online environment. Why the Youth Advisory Council Matters Young people are among the most active participants in today s digital environment. Social media platforms, online communities and digital communication increasingly influence how people form relationships, consume information and understand social and political issues. At the same time, young people may encounter challenges including: Online harassment and abuse Polarization Misogynistic content Extremist content Harmful online communities Stereotyping and discrimination Rapidly emerging online trends Other forms of digital harm Research into these issues can benefit from the direct perspectives of young people who understand how online culture develops and changes. The YAC therefore provides an opportunity for young people to contribute directly to research and help ensure that research questions and proposed solutions are relevant to real-world experiences. What Will Youth Advisory Council Members Do? Membership is intentionally designed to be a low-lift volunteer role . Members are not expected to undertake extensive research work outside the meetings. Instead, participants primarily contribute through their perspectives, discussion and feedback. Their responsibilities include: 1. Attend Quarterly-Style Virtual Meetings Members participate in virtual meetings approximately every two to three months . Meeting schedules are developed collaboratively with members, taking their availability into consideration. This makes the opportunity suitable for young people who may be studying, working or managing other responsibilities. 2. Share Your Perspective Members are expected to bring their personal perspectives and experiences to discussions. This could involve talking about how young people interact with online culture, discussing emerging trends or highlighting concerns that researchers may need to consider. 3. Respond to Research Prompts During meetings, members may be asked to respond to questions or research prompts. Participants can provide their thoughts based on their experiences and understanding of issues affecting young people. 4. Provide Feedback on Research YAC members may review and provide feedback on: Research questions Project findings Proposed solutions Emerging research priorities Their feedback can help researchers better understand whether their work reflects the realities experienced by young people. 5. Identify Emerging Concerns Members can help surface issues that may be affecting young people but have not yet received sufficient attention. This is particularly important in online environments, where trends and communities can develop quickly. Key Areas of Discussion The Youth Advisory Council will explore trends in online culture, including several sensitive and rapidly evolving areas. Online Polarization Online platforms can contribute to increasingly divided conversations and communities. YAC members may help researchers understand how polarization appears in young people s online experiences and how young people perceive these changes. Online Harms The council may discuss different forms of harm occurring in digital spaces. Young people s perspectives can help identify emerging problems and provide insight into how these experiences affect individuals and communities. Misogyny Misogynistic content and communities can have significant effects on online culture. YAC members can contribute perspectives that help researchers understand how young people encounter and respond to misogynistic ideas and behaviours online. Extremism The council may also discuss online extremism and emerging extremist trends. Young people s perspectives can help researchers better understand how online environments evolve and how harmful ideas may spread or influence young audiences. Emerging Online Trends The scope of the YAC is not limited to the issues currently identified. The council can also help identify new and emerging concerns affecting young people as online culture continues to change. What Is the Time Commitment? One of the key features of this opportunity is its low time commitment . Members meet virtually approximately every 2–3 months . Participants are expected to: Attend the scheduled meetings Prepare to contribute their perspectives Respond to research prompts Provide feedback during discussions There is no expectation that members work on projects outside the meetings . This makes the council potentially suitable for young people who want to contribute to meaningful research while continuing with university, employment, volunteering or other commitments. One-Year Membership YAC members serve for an initial one-year term . Members have the option to renew their membership once . Participants may also leave the council at any time. If a member decides to step down, they simply need to inform the team. This structure provides flexibility while allowing members to contribute meaningfully over an extended period. Is the Youth Advisory Council Paid? No. The YAC is an unpaid volunteer opportunity . There is no salary or stipend mentioned in the opportunity information. However, members have the opportunity to contribute directly to research, provide feedback to researchers and help shape work addressing important issues affecting young people. The experience may also provide an opportunity to develop skills in: Research engagement Communication Critical thinking Giving constructive feedback Advisory participation Understanding online social issues Collaborative discussion Support for Sensitive Discussions Some of the topics discussed by the Youth Advisory Council may be sensitive. These include issues such as online harms, misogyny, extremism and other difficult experiences. Participation in any particular discussion is entirely voluntary . Members can choose not to participate in a conversation if they do not feel comfortable discussing a particular subject. According to the opportunity information, support resources are shared with all members upon joining . This approach recognises that participants may have different experiences and comfort levels when discussing sensitive topics. Who Should Apply? The opportunity is particularly suited to young people who: Are between 18 and 24 years old Have an interest in online culture Want to contribute to research Are interested in issues affecting young people Have perspectives on digital communities and online experiences Want to help researchers better understand Gen Z experiences Can participate in virtual meetings every 2–3 months Are comfortable sharing perspectives and providing constructive feedback Applicants do not need to be professional researchers. The purpose of the council is specifically to bring young people s perspectives and lived experiences into the research process. How to Apply Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly. Applicants should apply by email. Application Email Applications should be sent to: perilresearch@american.edu Email Subject Line Use the following subject format: YAC Application First Name Last Name For example: YAC Application Jane Smith What to Include in Your Application Applicants should provide the following information: 1. First and Last Name Provide your full name. 2. Age You should state your current age. Applicants must fall within the specified 18–24 age range . 3. Location Provide your city and state . The supplied opportunity information specifically requests city and state rather than country or continent. 4. Why Are You Interested in Joining the YAC? Applicants should explain why they want to become a member of the Youth Advisory Council. The response must be no more than 300 words . A strong response could explain your interest in: Online culture Youth issues Research Digital communities Online harms Social issues Giving young people a voice Contributing to research and solutions 5. What Do You Hope to Get Out of the Experience? Applicants should explain what they hope to gain from participating in the council. This response should also be no more than 300 words . You might discuss goals such as developing research-related experience, learning from researchers, meeting other young people, contributing to meaningful projects or developing your communication and advisory skills. 6. Resume or CV Applicants should also attach their resume/CV . Application Review Process Applications are reviewed on a quarterly basis . The process includes: Submission of the application by email Review of applications Shortlisting of candidates Invitation to a short interview for shortlisted applicants Selection of Youth Advisory Council members Because applications are accepted on a rolling basis, interested applicants do not need to wait for a single annual application period. Is There an Application Deadline? There is no fixed deadline stated . Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly . This means interested applicants should consider applying as soon as possible rather than waiting for a specific closing date. Why Join the PERIL Youth Advisory Council? The YAC offers young people an opportunity to move beyond simply being subjects of research and instead become contributors to the research process. Members can help researchers understand what matters to young people and how emerging online issues are experienced in everyday life. The opportunity can provide participants with the chance to: Have their perspectives heard Contribute to research questions Give feedback on research findings Influence proposed solutions Help identify emerging issues Learn about research and advisory work Connect with other young people Contribute to discussions about safer online environments Perhaps most importantly, members can help ensure that research about young people is informed by young people themselves . Click HERE to read more. Conclusion The PERIL Youth Advisory Council provides an opportunity for young people aged 18–24 to contribute directly to research examining online culture, polarization, online harms, misogyny, extremism and other emerging issues. With only virtual meetings every two to three months and no expectation of work outside meetings, the YAC has been intentionally designed as a low-lift volunteer opportunity . Members serve for one year, with the possibility of one renewal, and can provide meaningful input into research questions, findings, proposed solutions and emerging concerns. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly , giving interested young people the opportunity to apply throughout the year. For young people who want their experiences and perspectives to play a role in shaping research and conversations about the digital world, the PERIL Youth Advisory Council offers a meaningful way to shape the conversation and advise the research . Click HERE for more volunteering opportunities. title: UfM Med Youth Lab 2026: Fully Sponsored Entrepreneurship Skills Programme in Italy
summary: The Union for the Mediterranean (UfM) has opened applications for the third edition of the UfM Med Youth Lab , an introductory entrepreneurship and employability skills programme for university students and recent graduates across the Euro-Mediterranean region. The programme is designed specifically for young people aged 18–29 who are curious about entrepreneurship but have little or no previous experience in the field. Up to 30 young participants will take part in online training between October and December 2026, followed by practical, in-person workshops in Palermo, Italy, from 14–16 December 2026 . Participation is free of charge , while selected participants from eligible countries will receive financial support covering travel, visa and accommodation costs for the in-person component. About the UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 The UfM Med Youth Lab is a skills-building initiative organised by the Union for the Mediterranean , with the support of the German Development Cooperation (GIZ) and in partnership with the University of Palermo . The 2026 edition focuses on introducing young people to foundational concepts in entrepreneurship and employability . Rather than requiring applicants to already have a business or extensive entrepreneurial experience, the programme specifically targets beginners who want to understand entrepreneurship and develop practical skills they can use in their academic, professional and community activities. Through expert-led sessions, non-formal education, teamwork and peer learning, participants will develop their entrepreneurial mindset and strengthen practical transferable skills. What Participants Will Learn During the programme, participants will develop foundational knowledge and skills in: Entrepreneurial thinking and mindset Innovation Basic financial literacy Communication Problem-solving Employability Teamwork and peer learning The programme is designed to build participants confidence and help them understand how entrepreneurial thinking can be applied to real-life challenges. Training of Trainers Approach A distinctive feature of the 2026 edition is its Training of Trainers approach . Participants will receive support to design a simple introductory awareness session about entrepreneurship. They will then be encouraged to share this knowledge with other young people at the national or local level in 2027 . Participants are not expected to become professional entrepreneurship trainers or experts. Instead, the programme aims to equip them with enough knowledge and confidence to act as peer facilitators , introducing basic entrepreneurship concepts within their communities. This approach allows the impact of the programme to extend beyond the 30 selected participants. Programme Components The UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 consists of three main components: 1. Online Training October–December 2026 Selected participants will participate in online learning sessions covering entrepreneurship, innovation, financial literacy, communication and problem-solving. 2. In-Person Workshops 14–16 December 2026 The in-person component will take place in Palermo, Italy . The workshops will provide participants with opportunities for practical learning, teamwork, peer exchange and interaction with other young people from across the Mediterranean. 3. Follow-Up Activities 2027 Following the main programme, participants will be encouraged to share their newly acquired knowledge through introductory entrepreneurship awareness sessions with peers in their communities. Who Can Apply? Applicants must meet the following requirements: Be 18–29 years old at the time of application. Be a national and resident of a UfM Member State . Be currently enrolled in a university programme or have graduated no more than one year before the application deadline . Hold a valid travel document, such as a passport. Have at least B2-level English or equivalent ability to actively participate in discussions and group activities. Have little or no significant previous knowledge, training or professional experience in entrepreneurship. Be fully available to participate in both the online training and the in-person workshops in Palermo. The programme is specifically designed for beginners . Applicants with significant previous entrepreneurship training, experience running or funding a start-up, or professional experience working with business-support organisations are not eligible for selection . Participants from the 2024 and 2025 editions may also apply, provided they meet all eligibility requirements for the 2026 edition. Eligible Countries Selected participants from the following countries are eligible for full sponsorship of travel, visa and accommodation expenses associated with the in-person programme: 🇦🇱 Albania 🇩🇿 Algeria 🇧🇦 Bosnia and Herzegovina 🇪🇬 Egypt 🇯🇴 Jordan 🇱🇧 Lebanon 🇱🇾 Libya 🇲🇷 Mauritania 🇲🇪 Montenegro 🇲🇦 Morocco 🇲🇰 North Macedonia 🇵🇸 Palestine 🇸🇾 Syria 🇹🇳 Tunisia 🇹🇷 Türkiye For selected participants from these countries, travel, visa fees and accommodation for the in-person component in Palermo will be covered. What Makes This Opportunity Valuable? The programme provides young people with an opportunity to gain practical entrepreneurship knowledge without requiring them to already have a business idea, start-up or extensive entrepreneurial background. Participants will also benefit from: Practical entrepreneurship and employability skills Exposure to innovation and entrepreneurial thinking Basic financial literacy Communication and problem-solving skills Peer learning with young people from across the Mediterranean International networking and regional cooperation Hands-on learning in Palermo Experience developing a peer-focused entrepreneurship awareness session The programme also provides an opportunity for participants to bring what they learn back to their own communities. Background of the Programme The UfM Med Youth Lab was first launched in Fes, Morocco, in November 2024 . Its second edition combined online training with in-person workshops in Tirana, Albania , in September and October 2025. The first two editions focused primarily on project-development skills , helping young people transform ideas into structured project proposals. Building on lessons from these previous editions, the 2026 programme introduces a new emphasis on entrepreneurship and employability skills , while maintaining the initiative s focus on practical learning, peer exchange and regional cooperation. The programme forms part of the UfM s broader work to strengthen youth participation, skills development and access to opportunities across the Euro-Mediterranean region . It contributes to the objectives of the UfM Youth Strategy 2030 and the UfM Youth Agenda: Call for Action , which highlight the importance of education, employment, social inclusion and meaningful youth participation. Application Process Before applying, candidates should: Check that they meet all eligibility requirements. Review the financial coverage available to participants. Carefully read the application guidelines. Prepare the required attachments. Submit the completed application before the deadline. Application Deadline 📅 30 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST How to Apply Interested applicants can submit their applications through the official UfM Med Youth Lab application platform: 🔗 Apply for the UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 For questions or difficulties with the application process, applicants can contact: medyouthlab@ufmsecretariat.org Conclusion The UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 offers a valuable opportunity for university students and recent graduates to gain foundational entrepreneurship and employability skills in an international learning environment. With free participation , online training, practical workshops in Palermo , and full travel, visa and accommodation support available to selected participants from eligible countries, the programme provides a strong opportunity for young people who are at the beginning of their entrepreneurial journey. Young people who meet the eligibility requirements and have little or no previous entrepreneurship experience are encouraged to apply before the 30 August 2026 deadline. title: Commonwealth Youth Council One Country, One Project 2026: Call for Applications
summary: The Commonwealth Youth Council (CYC) has launched One Country, One Project 2026 , a Commonwealth-wide initiative designed to recognise and showcase impactful youth-led projects that are responding to real challenges in communities. The initiative is being launched around International Youth Day 2026 , observed annually on 12 August . The United Nations has designated the 2026 theme as “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations,” highlighting the shared aspirations of young people across different countries and communities, including the desire for opportunity, meaningful participation, decent work, dignity and a sustainable future. What Is One Country, One Project? One Country, One Project is an initiative of the Commonwealth Youth Council , the official representative body of young people across the Commonwealth s 56 member states. According to the CYC, the initiative was developed around a simple principle: global problems require local solutions . The programme seeks to work with National Youth Councils and youth leaders in Commonwealth member countries to identify and support locally designed projects that benefit young people. For the 2026 call, youth-led organisations across the Commonwealth are invited to register projects that will be implemented between August and September 2026 . This creates an opportunity for organisations that are already working on community challenges—or are ready to implement a project during this period—to bring their work to the attention of a wider Commonwealth audience. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is intended for youth-led organisations across Commonwealth countries . Organisations should have a project that addresses a genuine challenge within their community and that can be implemented during the designated August–September 2026 period. The initiative is particularly relevant to youth organisations working on practical community solutions, social development, youth empowerment, employment, education, climate action, innovation, entrepreneurship, inclusion and other issues affecting young people. The CYC s broader programme description explains that the initiative will involve collaboration with National Youth Councils and youth leaders in member countries. What Kind of Projects Are Relevant? The initiative is focused on impactful, youth-led projects , rather than simply ideas that have not yet been put into practice. This means organisations should think about projects that can produce a clear and demonstrable benefit within their communities. Potential examples could include projects addressing: Youth unemployment and employability Entrepreneurship and economic empowerment Education and skills development Climate action and environmental sustainability Digital inclusion and technology Community health and wellbeing Social inclusion and equality Food security and sustainable livelihoods Community development Innovation and locally driven solutions The important consideration is not simply the size of the project, but the problem it addresses, the people it serves, what is implemented and the impact that can be demonstrated . Why This Opportunity Matters Youth-led organisations are often closest to the challenges affecting their communities. They understand local realities and can develop solutions that respond directly to those circumstances. This approach also fits closely with the focus of International Youth Day 2026 , which recognises that young people experience different social, economic and geographic realities while sharing common aspirations. The UN specifically highlights youth innovation and the importance of practical, creative solutions to local and global challenges. One Country, One Project therefore provides a platform for youth organisations to demonstrate that young people are not only beneficiaries of development programmes but also designers, implementers and leaders of solutions . Recognition and Commonwealth Best Project Award Following implementation, projects will be assessed based on their demonstrated impact . Outstanding projects will receive recognition at the country level and may be considered for the Commonwealth Best Project Award 2026 . This gives participating organisations an opportunity to gain recognition beyond their immediate community and potentially have their work highlighted at a major Commonwealth gathering. The award is expected to be presented during CHOGM Week in Antigua and Barbuda . The 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting will take place in St John s, Antigua and Barbuda, from 1–4 November 2026 . It will bring together representatives from the Commonwealth s 56 member countries, including government, business, civil society and youth organisations. Connection to Commonwealth Youth Engagement The initiative comes at an important time for youth participation within the Commonwealth. The 2026 Commonwealth Youth Forum (CYF) will also take place in Antigua and Barbuda alongside CHOGM. The forum is intended to provide young people with a platform to address issues affecting them and ensure that youth perspectives contribute to Commonwealth decision-making. The 2026 Commonwealth Youth Forum is being held under the theme “Investing in Youth Agency – Co-Creating Pathways towards Shared Prosperity.” A 23-member international taskforce has been selected to help shape and deliver the forum. Against this backdrop, One Country, One Project offers another avenue for youth-led action to be recognised within the wider Commonwealth youth agenda. How the Selection Process Works The process begins with project registration . After registration, participating organisations are expected to implement their projects during August and September 2026 . Projects will then be assessed based on the impact they have demonstrated. For organisations hoping to stand out, it will therefore be important to document their work carefully. Evidence could include the number of people reached, activities completed, outcomes achieved, community feedback, photographs, testimonials, partnerships and other measurable results. A strong project should be able to clearly answer three questions: What problem did you address? What did you do about it? What changed as a result? Application Deadline The deadline to register for One Country, One Project 2026 is 22 August 2026 . Youth-led organisations across Commonwealth member countries are encouraged to review the requirements and register their projects before the deadline. How to Register Official project registration page: Commonwealth Youth Council – Impact Projects The CYC s official impact-projects page confirms that One Country, One Project is being developed to support locally designed projects and that the Council intends to work with National Youth Councils on the initiative. ( Commonwealth Youth Council ) Conclusion The Commonwealth Youth Council s One Country, One Project 2026 is an opportunity for youth-led organisations to turn local action into wider recognition. Rather than focusing only on ideas, the initiative places emphasis on projects that are implemented and can demonstrate meaningful community impact . For organisations already working on practical solutions to challenges affecting young people, this could be an opportunity to showcase their work on a Commonwealth-wide platform. With projects scheduled for implementation between August and September 2026 , interested organisations should begin preparing immediately and ensure that their proposed project has clear objectives, beneficiaries, activities and measurable outcomes. The deadline for registration is 22 August 2026 . Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY webpage . title: WHO Africa and TDR Impact Grants 2026–2027: Call for Implementation Research for Regional Health Priorities
summary: The 2026–2027 Joint WHO African Region/TDR Impact Grants are now accepting applications for implementation research projects focused on addressing regional public health priorities in Africa. The initiative is jointly launched by the WHO Regional Office for Africa (AFRO) and TDR , the WHO-hosted Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases. It aims to strengthen health research capacity in developing countries while supporting research that can improve the delivery of high-quality and cost-efficient healthcare in resource-poor settings. About the Impact Grants The Impact Grants for Regional Priorities support implementation research that can help translate evidence, policies and health interventions into practical solutions that work in real-world settings. TDR explains that the programme is designed to strengthen the research capacity of individuals and institutions in countries, generate knowledge and implementation strategies that countries can apply, and encourage cooperation between researchers and national and international partners. The programme has focused on implementation research since 2014, with WHO regional offices working with TDR to identify research priorities relevant to their regions. Key Objectives The 2026–2027 call seeks to support public health-oriented implementation research that can contribute to stronger healthcare systems and better health outcomes. The initiative particularly aims to: Strengthen health research capacity in developing countries. Support researchers and institutions undertaking implementation research. Generate evidence that can improve the implementation of public health interventions. Develop practical and cost-efficient healthcare solutions for resource-poor settings. Support research addressing important regional health priorities. Encourage collaboration between researchers, health institutions and other relevant stakeholders. TDR s broader Impact Grants programme supports researchers and public health practitioners, including those working in ministries of health, academic institutions, research institutes, NGOs and professional or civil service organisations involved in relevant health research. What Is Implementation Research? Implementation research focuses on understanding how health interventions, programmes, policies and evidence can be effectively put into practice . Rather than simply asking whether a health intervention works, implementation research can examine questions such as: How can an effective intervention be delivered successfully in a particular community? What barriers prevent health programmes from reaching the people who need them? How can health services become more efficient and affordable? What approaches can help governments and health institutions implement evidence-based solutions? How can successful interventions be adapted to different local settings? This makes implementation research particularly important in settings where resources are limited and health systems must achieve the greatest possible impact with available resources. Who Can Apply? This opportunity is intended for health researchers, public health practitioners and relevant institutions in developing countries , particularly those working on implementation research connected to the African Region s public health priorities. Potential applicants may include professionals and researchers working through: Universities and academic institutions Research institutes Ministries of Health and public health programmes Tropical and communicable disease control programmes Non-governmental organisations Professional societies Civil service organisations involved in relevant health research TDR states that cooperation between researchers from different institutions, particularly collaboration involving researchers from more than one country, is strongly encouraged. Geographical eligibility: The call is focused on the WHO African Region , meaning applicants and research activities should meet the specific country and institutional eligibility requirements stated in the official 2026–2027 call documentation. The information provided for this announcement does not list the individual eligible countries or detailed institutional eligibility criteria , so applicants should consult the official call page before submitting a proposal. APPLY HERE Grant Focus The grants are intended to support public health-oriented implementation research that addresses identified regional priorities. Projects should therefore demonstrate a clear connection between the proposed research and practical health challenges affecting communities and health systems. Successful proposals should ideally demonstrate: A clearly defined public health problem. A strong implementation research question. Relevance to regional priorities. Potential to improve health service delivery or public health outcomes. A realistic research methodology. Potential for the findings to be applied by health systems or policymakers. Appropriate institutional capacity and partnerships. TDR notes that its Impact Grants are intended to produce research findings that can contribute to national strategies and action plans for controlling and treating diseases of poverty. Application Languages Applicants can submit their proposals in any of the following languages: English French Portuguese This provides researchers across the African Region with multiple options for preparing their applications. How to Apply Applications must be submitted electronically through the eTDR portal . Applicants should: Review the complete call documentation. Carefully check the eligibility requirements. Identify a research project that aligns with the stated regional priorities. Prepare the required proposal and supporting documentation. Ensure that all required information is complete. Submit the application through the eTDR portal before the deadline. Applications should be prepared carefully because competitive grant programmes generally require proposals to clearly demonstrate the relevance, feasibility and potential impact of the proposed research. Visit HERE to learn about the WHO Africa and TDR Impact Grants 2026–2027 Application Deadline The deadline for submitting applications is: 15 September 2026 at 17:00 CEST Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit before the final hours of the deadline to avoid technical problems or incomplete submissions. Why This Opportunity Matters The Impact Grants are particularly relevant for researchers who want their work to move beyond academic publication and contribute to real improvements in public health practice . TDR s Impact Grants have previously supported implementation research across different regions and have been used to strengthen links between research institutions, healthcare delivery and disease-control programmes. For African researchers, this type of funding can provide an opportunity to develop locally relevant evidence addressing challenges that may not be adequately captured by research conducted elsewhere. Conclusion The 2026–2027 Joint WHO African Region/TDR Impact Grants provide an opportunity for researchers and public health practitioners to develop implementation research addressing important health priorities in the African Region. The programme combines research capacity strengthening, evidence generation and practical health-system impact , making it particularly relevant to researchers whose work aims to improve how health interventions are delivered in resource-constrained settings. Eligible applicants should carefully review the full call requirements and submit their proposals through the eTDR portal before 15 September 2026 at 17:00 CEST . For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org. title: CIVICUS Global Digital Action Toolkit Consultancy 2026: Apply for a USD 9,000 Global Digital Rights and Activism Consultancy
summary: CIVICUS Global Digital Action Toolkit Consultancy 2026 CIVICUS Global Alliance is seeking an experienced consultant or consultancy team to develop a Global Digital Action Toolkit , a practical resource designed to help activists, civil society organisations, and citizens organise and participate in collective action in digital spaces safely, strategically, and effectively. The consultancy offers a contract worth up to USD 9,000 , inclusive of professional fees, taxes, and other associated costs. The selected consultant will work with CIVICUS to research, design, write, and finalise an approximately 15-page publication addressing digital organising, online mobilisation, digital protection, strategic communications, responsible digital storytelling, and impact measurement. The consultancy is expected to run for approximately three months, from mid-September to mid-November 2026 . About CIVICUS Global Alliance CIVICUS is a global alliance focused on defending and strengthening people power and civic action. The organisation brings together more than 17,000 members across more than 180 countries and works to protect civic freedoms, challenge violations, and strengthen the ability of people and civil society organisations to organise effectively. CIVICUS places particular emphasis on amplifying excluded and marginalised voices, especially those from the Global South. Through its work, CIVICUS supports efforts to create more accountable, effective, innovative, and inclusive civil society movements around the world. Background to the Global Digital Action Toolkit Digital platforms have become an increasingly important space for civic participation, activism, organising, advocacy, and public mobilisation. Activists and civil society organisations can use digital platforms to communicate with large audiences, coordinate campaigns, build movements, share information, document events, and advocate for social and political change. However, the growing importance of digital spaces has also created new challenges and risks. Activists increasingly face threats such as: Digital surveillance Internet shutdowns Disinformation Online harassment Platform restrictions Restrictions on digital communication Risks associated with organising online Challenges related to digital security and privacy CIVICUS already provides practical guidance for peaceful protest through its Global Protest Guide . However, there is a need for complementary guidance specifically focused on collective action that takes place in digital environments. The Global Digital Action Toolkit is intended to address this gap. The toolkit will provide practical guidance that helps activists and citizens understand how to plan and participate in digital assemblies and collective action while considering safety, strategy, communication, mobilisation, and impact. Purpose of the Consultancy The main purpose of this consultancy is to research, design, and develop a practical Global Digital Action Toolkit that provides actionable guidance for people organising collective action in digital spaces. The final resource should be practical rather than purely theoretical. It should combine useful recommendations with real-world examples and tools that activists and civil society organisations can apply in different contexts. The approximately 15-page publication is expected to include a combination of: Practical recommendations Case studies Examples Checklists Guidance Visual recommendations References Practical approaches to digital organising Information on digital protection and resilience The toolkit should be suitable for an international audience and recognise that activists operate in very different political, legal, social, and technological environments. Key Objectives of the Consultancy The selected consultant or consultancy team will be responsible for achieving several important objectives. 1. Develop practical written content The consultant will develop the main written content for the Global Digital Action Toolkit. The content should provide practical guidance that activists and civil society organisations can use when planning or participating in digital collective action. 2. Expand on the Global Protest Guide The toolkit should complement and expand the scope of CIVICUS s existing Global Protest Guide. Rather than duplicating existing guidance, the consultant should identify areas where digital collective action requires additional considerations and provide appropriate guidance. 3. Ensure global relevance The recommendations should be relevant to activists and civil society organisations operating across different regions of the world. The toolkit should recognise that digital organising can take place under very different conditions, including environments with: Strong civic freedoms Restricted civic space Internet shutdowns Government surveillance Platform restrictions Different legal frameworks Different levels of technological access Different levels of digital literacy 4. Make the toolkit practical and accessible The final publication should be easy for its intended users to understand and apply. The consultant should avoid creating a resource that is overly academic or theoretical. Instead, the toolkit should translate research and experience into clear recommendations and practical tools. Scope of Work The successful consultant will undertake research, writing, development, consultation, and revision activities throughout the assignment. Identify case studies and good practices The consultant will research relevant case studies, examples, and good practices that can strengthen the toolkit. These examples should help demonstrate how digital collective action works in different environments and what activists can learn from previous experiences. The research should contribute to a toolkit that is grounded in practical experience rather than general theory alone. Develop the Global Digital Action Toolkit The consultant will write the approximately 15-page toolkit. The publication is expected to address areas including: Digital organising and protection The toolkit should provide guidance on organising in digital environments while considering the safety, security, and resilience of participants. Online mobilisation The resource should explain practical approaches to mobilising people through digital platforms and building effective collective action online. Responsible digital storytelling The toolkit should address how activists and civil society organisations can use digital storytelling responsibly and strategically. This may include considerations around how stories are collected, presented, communicated, and shared. Strategic communications The consultant should provide guidance on developing effective communications strategies for digital collective action. This should help users communicate their objectives, reach relevant audiences, and strengthen their campaigns. Impact measurement The toolkit should provide practical approaches for understanding and measuring the impact of digital collective action. This could help activists and organisations assess whether their digital campaigns are achieving their intended objectives and identify areas for improvement. Expected Deliverables The selected consultant will be expected to produce several key deliverables during the consultancy. 1. Inception Concept Note and Toolkit Outline The first deliverable will establish the overall approach to the assignment. It should include: A proposed workplan The methodology that will be used The proposed structure of the toolkit An outline of the proposed content An approach to research and case-study identification This stage will provide CIVICUS with an opportunity to review and provide direction before the full toolkit is developed. 2. First Draft The consultant will prepare a complete first draft of the Global Digital Action Toolkit. The draft will be submitted to the CIVICUS team for review and feedback. It should demonstrate the proposed structure, content, practical recommendations, examples, and other relevant components of the final publication. 3. Final Toolkit The final deliverable will be a publication-ready Global Digital Action Toolkit of approximately 15 pages . The final version should incorporate feedback received from the CIVICUS team. It should also include suggested: Visuals Graphics References Layout approaches Other visual elements that could improve accessibility and usability The consultant is therefore expected not only to provide written content but also to offer recommendations that can assist a visual designer in turning the material into an engaging final publication. Consultancy Budget CIVICUS has allocated a total budget of up to USD 9,000 for this consultancy. The amount is inclusive of: Professional fees Taxes Other associated costs Applicants are required to submit a detailed financial proposal explaining their proposed consultancy fees and any anticipated expenses. Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed budget clearly reflects the complete cost of delivering the assignment. Consultancy Duration The consultancy is expected to run for approximately three months . The anticipated period is: Mid-September to Mid-November 2026 Applicants should take this timeframe into consideration when developing their proposed methodology, workplan, and budget. How to Apply Interested consultants or consultancy teams should submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) by email to: FoPA@civicus.org The email should use the following subject line: EOI Development of the Global Digital Action Toolkit The application must be received by: 28 August 2026 Applicants are encouraged to ensure that all required documents are complete and submitted before the deadline. Required Application Documents The application should comprise three documents . 1. Full CV Applicants should submit a full curriculum vitae outlining their professional background, relevant experience, qualifications, skills, and previous assignments. The CV should clearly demonstrate experience relevant to the consultancy. 2. Cover Letter The cover letter should be a maximum of two pages . It should: Introduce the applicant or consultancy team Describe relevant skills and experience Demonstrate understanding of the assignment Explain the proposed approach Describe how the assignment will be accomplished Highlight experience that makes the applicant or team suitable for the work Applicants should use the cover letter to demonstrate not only their qualifications but also their understanding of digital collective action and the needs of activists and civil society organisations. 3. Proposed Budget Applicants must provide a proposed financial budget for undertaking the assignment. The budget should clearly outline: Consultancy fees Anticipated expenses Any other relevant costs Since the maximum available budget is USD 9,000 inclusive of professional fees, taxes, and associated costs , applicants should ensure their proposal remains within the available budget. What the Successful Consultant Will Be Expected to Deliver The successful applicant will need to combine research, writing, strategic thinking, and an understanding of digital civic action. The assignment requires more than simply producing a written report. The final resource should be a practical toolkit that activists and civil society organisations can actually use. A strong approach would therefore need to consider: The realities of digital activism in different regions. The risks faced by activists using digital platforms. The opportunities created by online organising. Digital safety and resilience. Online mobilisation strategies. Responsible communications and storytelling. Strategic campaign communications. Methods for measuring digital campaign impact. Differences in political, legal, and technological environments. Accessibility and practical usability of the final toolkit. Why This Consultancy Is Important The increasing role of digital platforms in civic participation means that activists now need to understand both the opportunities and risks associated with digital collective action. Digital spaces can help movements reach audiences that may be difficult to reach through traditional forms of organising. They can also facilitate rapid mobilisation, information sharing, storytelling, advocacy, and international solidarity. At the same time, digital organising can expose activists and organisations to surveillance, misinformation, platform restrictions, online threats, and other challenges. A practical Global Digital Action Toolkit can therefore help bridge the gap between traditional guidance on civic action and the realities of contemporary digital organising. The resource will potentially provide activists and civil society organisations with practical knowledge that can be adapted to different contexts around the world. Who Can Apply? This opportunity is intended for qualified individual consultants or consultancy teams with relevant professional expertise and experience capable of researching and developing a global digital action resource. Particularly relevant backgrounds may include: Digital organising and activism Civil society and civic-space work Digital rights and digital security Strategic communications Advocacy and campaigning Research and case-study development Digital storytelling Civil society capacity building Development of toolkits, guides, publications, or similar resources The Terms of Reference do not specify a particular nationality, race, ethnicity, or continent as an eligibility restriction . The assignment is designed for a global audience, and applicants should demonstrate the relevant expertise and experience required to successfully undertake the consultancy. Interested applicants should nevertheless review the complete Terms of Reference and application requirements carefully before submitting their Expression of Interest. Visit HERE to learn more about the How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Application Applicants interested in this consultancy should ensure that their application directly responds to the requirements in the Terms of Reference. A strong application should clearly demonstrate relevant experience rather than relying only on general professional qualifications. Applicants can strengthen their submission by: Clearly explaining previous experience with digital organising, civic action, communications, advocacy, activism, or civil society. Providing relevant examples of research, publications, toolkits, guides, campaigns, or similar resources they have developed. Demonstrating experience working with international or geographically diverse audiences. Showing an understanding of digital safety and resilience. Explaining their methodology for identifying credible case studies and good practices. Presenting a realistic workplan for the three-month consultancy. Providing a clear and detailed financial proposal. Explaining how feedback from CIVICUS will be incorporated into subsequent drafts. Demonstrating the ability to produce accessible and practical content. Highlighting experience working with visual designers or preparing content that can easily be translated into visually engaging publications. Important Dates and Application Information Item Details Organisation CIVICUS Global Alliance Opportunity Development of the Global Digital Action Toolkit Opportunity type Consultancy Budget Up to USD 9,000 Consultancy duration Approximately 3 months Expected period Mid-September to mid-November 2026 Toolkit length Approximately 15 pages Application method Expression of Interest by email Application email FoPA@civicus.org Email subject EOI Development of the Global Digital Action Toolkit Application deadline 28 August 2026 Required documents Full CV, maximum two-page cover letter, proposed budget Conclusion The CIVICUS Global Digital Action Toolkit Consultancy 2026 presents an opportunity for an experienced consultant or consultancy team to contribute to an important global resource focused on digital civic action. With a budget of up to USD 9,000 , the assignment involves researching good practices, developing practical guidance, producing an approximately 15-page toolkit, incorporating feedback from CIVICUS, and delivering a publication-ready manuscript with recommendations for visuals and layout. The consultancy is particularly relevant to professionals with experience in digital activism, civil society, civic space, advocacy, strategic communications, digital organising, research, digital rights, campaign development, or related fields . Interested applicants should carefully prepare the three required application documents and submit their Expression of Interest to FoPA@civicus.org using the subject line “EOI Development of the Global Digital Action Toolkit” . The application deadline is 28 August 2026 , with the consultancy expected to take place from mid-September to mid-November 2026 . For more Global consultancy opportunity visit OFY HERE .
